price.headline: Bespoke timber verandas from about €5,000 plus VAT.
price.note: The final price depends on size, finish and specification. Glass rooms and fully enclosed rooms are a different specification and cost considerably more, so we price them per project.

process.title: Tell us what you want
process.text: Send photos of the garden, rough sizes and whether you want it open or enclosed.

process.title: Visit and design
process.text: We check the site, confirm whether Class 3 or the extension rules apply, and agree the design.

process.title: Detailed written quotation
process.text: You receive a written quotation for the structure, glazing and any outdoor kitchen.

process.title: Build
process.text: Our crew builds the timber frame, roof and glazing on site.

faqs.a: It depends on whether the structure is detached or attached. A detached structure is assessed under the Class 3 limits; one attached to the house is treated as an extension. We check your site first, and a Section 5 declaration from the council gives certainty.

faqs.q: Can I start open and enclose it later?
faqs.a: Talk to us at design stage. Planning for sliding glass from the start keeps the options open.

faqs.q: Are your verandas timber or aluminium?
faqs.a: Timber. Our verandas and glass rooms are timber-framed.

faqs.q: Can you build an outdoor kitchen inside it?
faqs.a: Yes. We have built outdoor rooms with built-in kitchens, bars and BBQs, including the one in Ashbourne.

faqs.q: Do you work in my area?
faqs.a: We work within 50 km of Dunshaughlin, Co. Meath. That covers all of Dublin and towns in Meath, Kildare, Louth (such as Drogheda) and north Wicklow.

cta.title: Planning a veranda or glass room?
cta.text: Send us photos of the garden and rough sizes, and tell us whether you want it open or enclosed. We will visit and prepare a detailed written quotation.

sections.title: Planning: detached or attached
paragraphs: A detached timber veranda or glass room is assessed under the Class 3 limits for garden structures. One attached to the house is treated as an extension, with its own rules.
Either may be exempt if it meets the conditions. We check your site first.
